# QC07: 涵秋馆 Hanqiu Guan

Wave 4 · Qichun Yuan · 3D: `/reconstruction/3d.html?b=QC07` · Page: `/scenes/#QC07` · Row: `research/buildings/QC07-hanqiu-guan/`

## What it was

涵秋馆 Hanqiu Guan, "Hall Holding Autumn", on a long north-south island north-west of 敷春堂, about 200 by 60 m, with lake to the east and north, facing 凤麟洲 to the east, planted for autumn colour (E0663, E0660). Begun early in Jiaqing's reign (about 1805, added 1810): a south-facing seven-bay double 工字 hall, front and rear halls with galleries, and a rockwork fountain between them fed by a raised tank east of the wall (E0660, E0661, E0662). The 'autumn' of the four season halls (E0661). Near it stood 仙人承露台, a bronze immortal on a high platform, whose base is now in 中山公园 (E0662). Burned on 18 October 1860 (E0680).

From the inventory row: **built** 嘉庆十年七月 1805; added to 1809; about 1805, added 1810; early Jiaqing; **destroyed** 1860 (S06, S42, S52, S01, S220, S227, S339, S361).

## What survives today

A 2007 survey west of 仙人承露台 covered about 2,586 m2 (55-74 by 26-48 m) with two stone stairs on the north and west (E0664, E0665); results paywalled. Service buildings stood on it about 2011 (E1011).
